 NFL schedule flex: League moves Week 12 'Sunday Night Football' matchup, shifts afternoon games
 Patriots at Chargers is moving out of primetime
 By
 Jordan Dajani 
 Nov 17, 2026
 at
 2:24 pm ET 
 •
 4 min read
 Getty Images 
 The NFL is flexing its scheduling freedom, moving the Week 12 Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland Browns matchup from 1 p.m. ET to "Sunday Night Football." The New England Patriots were originally scheduled to play the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in primetime that week, but that matchup will now move to 4:05 p.m. ET. 
 Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars , which was originally scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET that week moves to 1 p.m. ET.
 The Raiders-Browns matchup will feature Las Vegas's newest quarterback, Fernando Mendoza . The No. 1 overall pick took over after Vegas (4-6) sent Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the trade deadline last Tuesday, and Week 12 will mark the first primetime matchup of his career. Mendoza completed 17-of-29 passes for 143 yards in his first career start on Sunday, which came in a 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks . 
 As for the Browns, they moved to 6-4 last week following a remarkable comeback win over the Houston Texans . The 17-0 deficit Deshaun Watson and Co. overcame made it the second-largest comeback win at home in franchise history, while the Browns are now a perfect 4-0 in their home stadium for the first time since 1963. Cleveland currently holds the last wild-card spot in the AFC (No. 7 seed), behind the 6-3 Pittsburgh Steelers and 7-2 Denver Broncos .
 The 5-5 Patriots are being flexed out of primetime following their disastrous 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. The team fears that quarterback Drake Maye , who suffered a lower-leg injury early in the game, could be sidelined for an extended period of time, according to ESPN . The injury could force last year's MVP runner-up to miss the remainder of the season. New England's Week 12 opponent, the Chargers, actually just tallied their first win of the season on Monday night, defeating  Jacoby Brissett's   Baltimore Ravens , 23-20.
 The NFL implemented this "flexible scheduling" rule in 2006. For "Sunday Night Football," they can flex up to two games between Weeks 5-10 and any week during Weeks 11-17.
